messages:
Maya (eng-runtime): @channel customer flagged a big tail latency spike after the runtime rollout we started ~11:10 UTC. p95 normally ~320ms, p99 jumped to ~1.6s for their traffic. they opened a ticket, escalating to SEs.
Jason (eng-sre): which rollout id? did we do a full deploy or staged?
Maya (eng-runtime): rollout id rtime-2.8.3, staged to ~25% traffic (staged routing policy). started at 11:05, errors are not increasing but tail only. no obvious 5xx.
Oliver (support): customer says spikes affect inference latency for sequences >512 tokens, but short requests ok. they provided sample request ids. attaching logs now.
support-bot: attached logs: request_ids: [req-8471, req-8478, req-8480] (see ticket #CUST-998).
Samira (eng-runtime): pushing traces now from the nodes that handled those req ids. preliminary flamegraph shows long time in kernel launch / attention kernel (~600-800ms) on a subset of GPU nodes.
Jason (eng-sre): do we have perf counters for those nodes? queueing/serialize time or just GPU compute time?
Samira (eng-runtime): counters show GPU compute time increased but also scheduling wait increased (~200ms) on the same pods. interestingly only pods on hostpool-eu-west-2a show it.
Priya (eng-platform): did the rollout change any batching or scheduling defaults? the v2.8 release had a scheduling tweak: dynamic_batching.delay_ms default changed 6->12 for throughput.
Maya (eng-runtime): yes we bumped dynamic_batching delay to be more aggressive for throughput; that should increase batch sizes and reduce cost, but could hurt latency for some workloads.
Oliver (support): customer workload is bursty with many short + occasional long sequences. larger batches might delay those long requests behind short ones?
Jason (eng-sre): that matches head-of-line blocking. Also Samira mentioned increased attention kernel time — could be model variant quantization/attention change + bigger batches.
Samira (eng-runtime): I pulled model variant mapping: affected nodes used model-variant v3-fused-attn (new compiled kernel) that we rolled alongside the runtime (compat build). older nodes still on v3-legacy-attn.
Maya (eng-runtime): hypothesis: the new fused-attn kernel has worse tail for long sequences at high batch sizes and the scheduling change pushed more requests into those batches, exposing the regression.
Jason (eng-sre): plan: (1) immediately route customer traffic away from nodes running rtime-2.8.3 / fused-attn to older pool; (2) rollback scheduling change in canary; (3) bisect the fused-attn change commit range to find culprit; (4) communicate to customer. who's on rollback?
Priya (eng-platform): I can alter routing policy to exclude pool: rtime-2.8.3-eu-west-2a. doing it now: command: 
```
redwoodctl routing update --exclude-pool rtime-2.8.3-eu-west-2a --reason "p99 spike" --ticket CUST-998
```

Priya (eng-platform): applied. traffic for that customer should flow to rtime-2.7.* in ~30s.
deploy-bot: routing update accepted, change id route-5521, propagated to edge in 22s.
Maya (eng-runtime): can we temp disable increased delay to reduce batch buildup while we bisect?
Priya (eng-platform): yes — lowering dynamic_batching.delay_ms back to 6 on canary nodes now. command: 
```
redwoodctl config set --pool rtime-2.8.3-eu-west-2a dynamic_batching.delay_ms=6
```

Priya (eng-platform): done, change id cfg-9983.
Samira (eng-runtime): rechecking metrics: customer p99 dropped from 1.6s -> ~360ms within two minutes after routing change + config tweak. looks promising.
Oliver (support): updated customer: "We've routed you to previous pool and applied a temporary scheduling tweak; monitoring now. We'll follow up with root cause." They acknowledged, sent logs.
Jason (eng-sre): next: bisect fused-attn commits. Samira, can you start a git bisect on the fused-attn repo branch that shipped with v2.8.3? include kernel patch set + compiler flags. record the known-good commit (rtime-2.7 tag) and known-bad (rtime-2.8.3).
Samira (eng-runtime): starting bisect locally against the compiled kernel suite. steps I'm using: 
```
git checkout -b bisect-fused-attn rtime-2.7
git bisect start rtime-2.8.3 rtime-2.7
# build and run microbench that simulates long seqs + batching
./bench/run_attention_bench --seq-len 1024 --batch-dist "bursty"
# mark good/bad accordingly
```

Samira (eng-runtime): initial passes show commit range 7a1f..c3d2 narrows to two commits that touch kernel launch parameters and padding.
Maya (eng-runtime): do we have reproducible microbench results? customer quantization/variant details?
Oliver (support): customer uses model v3-large-quant (int8). provided model sha.
Samira (eng-runtime): microbench with same quant flags reproduces the regression on kernels when batch sizes >8 and seq>512. the suspect commit adjusts per-thread tile sizes in fused kernel.
Jason (eng-sre): great find. next step: roll-forward fix or revert kernel change for the fused-attn build. which is faster? revert is faster.
Maya (eng-runtime): let's prepare a hotfix build that reverts the tile-size commit and publish a patched runtime 2.8.3-hotfix. Samira, can you build and smoke test? Priya, can you stage rollout?
Samira (eng-runtime): building artifact now. will run the attention bench (seq 1024, batch burst) + end-to-end inference smoke on canary nodes.
Priya (eng-platform): once Samira posts green, I'll create staged rollout to 20% on eu-west and monitor p99 for 30m before broader rollout.
Samira (eng-runtime): bench green locally. smoke tests on canary pool pass. artifact sha: af3b9c.
deploy-bot: artifact af3b9c uploaded to registry.
Priya (eng-platform): staging rollout started to 20% eu-west pools with new artifact 2.8.3-hotfix. monitoring dashboards: p95/p99 trending down on canary shards.
Jason (eng-sre): after we confirm for 30 mins, escalate to full rollout. Also add a temporary guard in runtime to limit batch size for sequences >512 until we validate.
Maya (eng-runtime): I'll update the incident note and prepare a short RCA draft: root cause = fused-attn kernel tile-size change regressed long-sequence tail when paired with increased batching delay; mitigations = routing away, config rollback, hotfix rebuild; follow-ups = add microbench for long-tail sequences in our presubmit, add e2e canary checks for p95/p99 on sequence distributions, and update rollback playbook.
Oliver (support): customer replied: "Thanks — latencies back to expected levels, appreciate quick response." closing their P1 for now, will reopen if regressions return.
Samira (eng-runtime): action items assigned in incident doc: bisect notes, tests to add, PR to revert tile-size commit + unit perf tests.
Maya (eng-runtime): thanks everyone. we'll keep this thread updated if anything changes.
Jason (eng-sre): quick notes for postmortem: include timeline, config diff (delay_ms change), kernel commit id (c3d2xx), hotfix sha (af3b9c), routing change id (route-5521). Also add metric screenshots.
Maya (eng-runtime): adding those to the incident doc now.
Samira (eng-runtime): leaving final note: if anyone sees similar tail spikes, check pool mapping -> model-variant -> batching config first. that triad caused the user-visible issue.
Maya (eng-runtime): ack. closing thread for now.
